descriptionChirho: Moral badness, sinfulness, or wickedness as a quality or abstract concept, often in construct with a possessor or used attributively.
An external catastrophe, disaster, or judgment brought upon people, often by God; translating as calamity, disaster, or doom rather than moral evil.
Affliction, suffering, or distress experienced by a person, emphasizing the subjective hardship rather than moral fault or external catastrophe.
Plural concrete acts of evil, wicked deeds, or a collection of bad things done, referring to specific sinful actions rather than abstract wickedness.
Damage, harm, or hurt intended or inflicted upon a specific person, focusing on the injurious effect rather than moral quality or divine judgment.
